name: The Palazzo at the Venetian
positioning: The Palazzo at The Venetian Resort, on the north-center Las Vegas Strip, shares a complex with The Venetian and the Grand Canal Shoppes; its suites start at 720 square feet
best_for: Travelers wanting a suite with a marble bathroom, a workspace and a separate living area
Couples wanting a suite with a sunken living room or views of the Sphere
Spa-goers wanting access to Canyon Ranch Spa + Fitness

facts.text: The Palazzo is on the north-center Las Vegas Strip, sharing a complex with The Venetian and the Grand Canal Shoppes.
Guests can walk indoors between the Palazzo and Venetian towers and use all of The Venetian's amenities.
Every suite has a marble bathroom, a workspace, a living area and a pillow-top bed.
The Luxury King Suite Sphere View has views of the Sphere at The Venetian.
The Grand One Bedroom King Suite has a double-door entrance, a marble foyer, a living area, a dining table for four and a private bedroom with one king bed.
Prestige Club Lounge suites include a welcome glass of prosecco at check-in, a personal concierge and breakfast.
The resort has heated swimming pools.
TAO Beach is a pool deck with live DJ sets and drinks.
The Palazzo Casino Floor offers a full range of casino games and a high-limit lounge.
The Palazzo has Silver LEED certification and energy-efficient systems.
The Grand Canal Shoppes are downstairs from the Palazzo.
WAKUDA in The Palazzo Lobby serves sushi, with a late-night dinner menu and an omakase experience.

highlights.text: The Palazzo Luxury King Suite Strip View has a sunken living room and a Roman tub.
Suites at The Palazzo start at 720 square feet.
Guests can take an indoor or outdoor gondola ride on a rendition of the Grand Canal inspired by the waterway of Venice.
Guests have access to Canyon Ranch Spa + Fitness, with climbing walls, hydrotherapy and wellness consults.
Prestige-level suites have access to the 23rd-floor lounge, with breakfast, evening bites and Strip views.

considerations.text: Refrigerators in the suites carry an additional charge.
Conde Nast Traveler says the Palazzo is family friendly but the overall vibe skews more grown-up.
WhataHotel notes the busy Strip location brings high tourist traffic.
